description: Machine-readable enforcement map for the rules in context.md. Every rule is owned by one or more deterministic layers; 'llm' marks the judgment that remains after the scripts have run. AI assistants: never assert that a rule with a deterministic owner passes or fails by reading code — run the owning checker and report its output.

layers.lint: Framework ESLint a11y plugin plus built-in a11y-sdk source contract checks, run by the pre-commit hook on staged files (scripts/pre-commit.cjs).
layers.llm: LLM or human judgment at generation/review time — cannot be automated.

rules.title: Non-text Content
rules.llmJudgment: Is the alt text meaningful? Is a decorative image correctly aria-hidden?

rules.title: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
rules.llmJudgment: axe:audio-caption only flags a bare <audio>/<video> with no transcript sibling detectable in markup (and is itself a deprecated axe rule) — whether a real text transcript or audio description actually exists and is adequate is entirely judgment. See the Media, Timing & Motion section in context.md.

rules.title: Captions (Prerecorded)
rules.llmJudgment: axe:video-caption only flags a <video> with no <track kind="captions"> element at all — whether captions that DO exist are accurate and complete is entirely judgment.

rules.title: Info and Relationships
rules.llmJudgment: Do the chosen semantics actually match the visual structure? (axe:heading-order/region/landmark-* are best-practice-tagged rules force-enabled on top of the WCAG tag filter — see audit.ts's BEST_PRACTICE_RULES.) behave:visual-headings narrows this to a short candidate list of visually-prominent non-heading text — deciding which candidates are genuinely acting as headings (vs. a stat tile, CTA, or pull-quote) stays judgment, which is why that recipe only warns.

rules.title: Meaningful Sequence
rules.llmJudgment: Does DOM order match reading order where CSS repositions content (flex order, absolute positioning)?

rules.title: Identify Input Purpose
rules.llmJudgment: Is the chosen autocomplete token the semantically correct one for the field?

rules.title: Use of Color
rules.llmJudgment: axe:link-in-text-block only catches the specific case of an in-text link with no non-color distinction (underline, weight) from surrounding text. Whether any OTHER information is conveyed by color alone, without a text/icon/pattern counterpart, remains judgment.

rules.title: Resize Text
rules.llmJudgment: Font sizes computed at runtime (dynamic style objects, CSS-in-JS templates) escape the static px check.

rules.title: Non-text Contrast
rules.llmJudgment: Do UI component boundaries and focus indicators reach 3:1 against adjacent colors? (Not automated.)

rules.title: Content on Hover or Focus
rules.llmJudgment: Are tooltips dismissible, hoverable, and persistent?

rules.title: Keyboard
rules.llmJudgment: Is every mouse-available action of a custom widget genuinely operable by keyboard? (Reachability of ARIA-interactive elements and Tab/Shift+Tab symmetry are now script-verified.)

rules.title: No Keyboard Trap
rules.llmJudgment: Traps outside dialogs that don't manifest as forward/backward asymmetry (e.g. embedded third-party widgets) need manual keyboard testing.

rules.title: Timing Adjustable
rules.llmJudgment: axe:meta-refresh only catches a <meta http-equiv="refresh"> redirect/reload. Session timeouts and other script-driven timing live entirely in judgment — see the Media, Timing & Motion section in context.md.

rules.title: Pause, Stop, Hide
rules.llmJudgment: axe:blink/marquee only catch the deprecated HTML elements. CSS/JS-driven auto-updating carousels, animations, and moving content need a pause/stop/hide control that's entirely judgment to verify — see the Media, Timing & Motion section in context.md.

rules.title: Focus Order
rules.llmJudgment: behave verifies structural symmetry (Tab retraces Shift+Tab) and flags positive tabindex; whether the resulting order is meaning-preserving for the visual layout is still judgment.

rules.title: Link Purpose
rules.llmJudgment: Does the link text describe the destination (no 'click here' / 'read more')? behave:unique-labels catches the specific, well-documented failure of identical link text pointing to different destinations; whether the text is descriptive at all remains judgment.

rules.title: Headings and Labels
rules.llmJudgment: Do headings describe the content that follows? Do labels describe the input's purpose? (Presence of an h1, empty headings, and skipped levels are now script-verified.) Whether a flagged visual-headings candidate should actually become a real heading element is judgment. behave:unique-labels catches distinct form fields sharing an accessible name — whether an individual label's wording is descriptive remains judgment.

rules.title: Focus Appearance (WCAG 2.2)
rules.llmJudgment: behave verifies an indicator exists; the 2px-perimeter and 3:1-contrast requirements are not automated.

rules.title: Target Size (Minimum) (WCAG 2.2)
rules.llmJudgment: behave fails an undersized target only when it's crowded enough that even the spacing exception can't apply, and warns otherwise — whether an isolated undersized target genuinely qualifies for the spacing, inline-text, essential-presentation, or user-agent-control exception is judgment.

rules.title: Language of Page
rules.llmJudgment: Is the declared language code the actual content language?

rules.title: On Focus
rules.llmJudgment: Does receiving focus trigger any unexpected context change (submit, navigation)?

rules.title: On Input
rules.llmJudgment: Does changing a field auto-submit or navigate without warning?

rules.title: Error Identification
rules.llmJudgment: behave verifies aria-invalid="true" pairs with a real, non-empty aria-describedby once the field is in an error state; whether the error TEXT accurately describes the problem, and whether validation is triggered app-appropriately, remain judgment.

rules.title: Labels or Instructions
rules.llmJudgment: Is the label text a useful description of the input's purpose? (Presence of an accessible name and fieldset/legend grouping for radio groups are now script-verified.)

rules.title: Name, Role, Value
rules.llmJudgment: Does a custom widget expose ALL of its states, not just the ones linters can see declared? behave:unique-labels flags repeated button names as a warn (real severity varies too much for a hard fail — a card-grid "Add to cart" pattern is common and lower-risk than a form-field or link collision).

rules.title: Status Messages
rules.llmJudgment: Is the alert/status role choice appropriate for the urgency? Is content injected into a pre-existing container (not created simultaneously)?

patterns.llmJudgment: Nothing — the full contract (aria-modal, name, focus trap, Escape, focus restore) is script-verified. Pass --dialog-trigger when auto-detection can't open it.
Whether the error TEXT content accurately explains the problem; grouping strategies beyond simple same-name radio groups (e.g. checkbox groups, multi-field address blocks) still need a human read.
Complex spanning tables: are id/headers associations correct?
Is the Tab-model vs arrow-key-model choice appropriate? (aria-current="page" on the active link is now script-verified for any nav link that resolves to the current page's URL.)
Urgency-to-role mapping; injection timing; no stacked alerts within 1–2s.
